original_question: Let Γ be the first Grigorchuk group, viewed inside its profinite completion PF(Γ). Determine whether there exists an element g in PF(Γ) but not in Γ such that the subgroup ∆ generated by Γ and g has the congruence subgroup property. Producing such an element would give a new example of a non-isomorphic inclusion ψ: Γ -> ∆ whose induced map on profinite completions PF(ψ) is an isomorphism.
target_in_paper: Section 4, item (4.H), labeled "Open problem," with its follow-up use in Section 7, item (7.A) (Hypothesis/Lemma/Consequence).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the first Grigorchuk group inside its profinite completion, looks for an element outside the group that generates a proper overgroup inside that completion, and ties the existence of such an overgroup to producing a non-isomorphic inclusion whose induced map on profinite completions is an isomorphism. It also correctly focuses on the Grigorchuk-group-specific construction discussed in the paper rather than broadening to unrelated Grothendieck-pair questions.
missing_details: The paper does not ask for the classical congruence subgroup property; it asks for the congruence extension property, defined in Section 4, item (4.G): every normal subgroup N of the dense subgroup Δ must be of the form N = M ∩ Δ for some open normal subgroup M of the ambient profinite group.

The ambient profinite group should be identified exactly as PF(G), which for the first Grigorchuk group coincides with its pro-2 completion P̂_2(G), and also with its closure Ḡ in Aut(T), where T is the rooted dyadic tree.
The paper states the problem for the first Grigorchuk group G itself (not an arbitrary Γ), and the desired element lies in the complement PF(G) \ G.

The subgroup generated by G and g is automatically dense in PF(G), because it contains the canonical dense image of G; this density is implicit in the paper's setup and important for applying Section 4, items (4.G) and (4.H).

The subgroup Δ = ⟨G, g⟩ is automatically finitely generated, since G is finitely generated and only one extra element is adjoined; the paper's later hypothesis in Section 7, item (7.A) explicitly assumes such a finitely generated proper subgroup.

To make the question stand alone, one should state the exact motivation supplied by the paper: finding such a Δ would yield a new example of a non-isomorphic homomorphism ψ: G → Δ for which PF(ψ) is an isomorphism.
If one wants to align fully with the paper's later discussion, one should also mention the Section 7, item (7.A) consequence: under this hypothesis, PS(ψ): PS(G) → PS(Δ) would also be an isomorphism.

The appendix is relevant context: the paper says it gives an effective way to construct elements of Ḡ, including elements not in G, so the issue is not existence of elements outside G in the closure, but whether one can choose such an element so that the generated subgroup has the congruence extension property.
refined_question: Let G be the first Grigorchuk group, identified with its canonical dense image in its profinite completion PF(G) (equivalently, in its pro-2 completion P̂_2(G) = Ḡ ⊂ Aut(T), where T is the rooted dyadic tree). Does there exist an element g ∈ PF(G) \ G such that the proper finitely generated dense subgroup Δ := ⟨G, g⟩ has the congruence extension property, i.e. for every normal subgroup N ◁ Δ there exists an open normal subgroup M ◁ PF(G) with N = M ∩ Δ?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist a proper finitely generated dense subgroup G < Δ < PF(G) such that the inclusion Δ ↪ PF(G) induces an isomorphism PF(Δ) → PF(G)? In that case, the inclusion ψ: G ↪ Δ would be a non-isomorphism with PF(ψ) an isomorphism.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's explicit open problem in Section 4, item (4.H): to find an element g outside the first Grigorchuk group but inside its profinite completion so that the subgroup generated by G and g has the congruence extension property. That is the paper's nearest official formulation, and it already includes the exact Grothendieck-pair motivation your draft mentions. The draft is close, but it replaces the paper's key term "congruence extension property" by "congruence subgroup property," which is a different notion. Section 4, item (4.G) supplies the precise definition and the equivalence with an isomorphism on profinite completions for dense subgroups of finitely generated profinite groups. Section 7, item (7.A) then reuses exactly this existence statement as a hypothesis and shows why the authors care about it: if such a subgroup Δ exists, then finite quotients and soluble quotients of Δ coincide in the relevant sense, and the induced map on true prosoluble completions is also an isomorphism. The appendix confirms that the paper can effectively construct many elements of the closure Ḡ, including elements outside G, so the open issue is specifically the congruence extension property, not merely finding g ∉ G.
